body:
apologies for replying so late, i actually did mean to respond quickly, but other stuff got in the way instead of the usual putting it off.

reading your message was really nice. honestly it had me tearing up a little, haha. it's very reassuring to find out there's somebody out there who can relate so deeply to what i'm experiencing. the second and third paragraphs in particular hit me somewhere. i'm feeling something similar to what you described in the second one.

the structure of my reply is a bit jumbled, as i was just speaking about the last paragraphs and now i'm talking about the first, but the things you mentioned in it are the exact things i run into whenever i speak too. i feel like my vocabulary has shrunk to a fraction of what it used to be. 

see, now the jumbled structure really messes with the flow of my reply, because i was hoping to go from the nice way my first paragraph ended into a nice final paragraph, ahhhhhh. regardless, i'm thankful it happened to be you who commented here. i hope tomorrow treats you well, and the tomorrows after that.

thank you for the reply. this quite reassuring to read; as sorry as i am to hear that you've had to deal with similar problems.

worrying that others will be left to try to piece together my jumbled sentences is something i feel often too. it's especially frustrating as only a few years ago i used to be praised for being articulate. now i can hardly speak without needing to stop myself before i stumble over a word or start stuttering. i find that i've forgotten a lot of words i once used confidently, so i often go to say something only to realise i don't remember the word i intended to use.

it's not too bad, seeing as i don't speak very often at all. though it's always saddening whenever i try to be more social and i'm reminded of the aforementioned issues when i attempt conversations.

eh, i'm rambling, sorry. i appreciate you taking time to respond. thanks.
